    LengthSquared(self: Vector2D): Number
        => self.X.Square + self.Y.Square;

## Line 263

**Source:** [stdlib/foundation/vectors.library.plato, line 263](../../../../../stdlib/foundation/vectors.library.plato#L263).

```plato

    //==
    // # Portable bodies for the numeric tuples
    //
    // The concrete per-component operations on Number2 / Number3 / Number4 /
    // Number8 (`vectors.types.plato`). These used to be bodiless
    // declarations in `intrinsics.library.plato` forwarded to System.Numerics;
    // they are ordinary Plato now, so the host contract mentions only primitive
    // types. A backend may still substitute a native vector instruction for any of
    // them through its representation map and override table — these bodies define
    // what that substitution must compute.
    //
    // The generic component-wise surface in
    // `numeric-structures.library.plato` computes the same values through
    // Map/Zip over ComponentArray; the fixed-arity bodies here are the ones a
    // backend can map onto a single SIMD instruction, and they are written out lane
    // by lane for exactly that reason.
    //
    // Semantics match System.Numerics: Multiply and Divide of two tuples are
    // component-wise (Hadamard), never a dot product; Length is the Euclidean norm;
    // Clamp / Min / Max act per component; Number4.Transform follows the ROW-vector
    // convention v' = v M (CONVENTIONS.md - Matrices).

    //==
    // # Number2

    // The squared Euclidean length; avoids the square root.
    LengthSquared(self: Number2): Number
        => self.X * self.X + self.Y * self.Y;
```
